answer: Latency-bandwidth handshake gating. Each new identity must complete a random-duration challenge whose reply timing must fit a comet-shaped traffic curve: fast initial burst, long decay tail. The relay caps accepted handshakes per source to that curve, so a falcon-style spoof that answers instantly and uniformly gets rejected as too regular. Every accepted identity thus costs the attacker real sustained bandwidth and idle time across days; a surviving relic identity carries that recorded timing fingerprint into later traffic.
